title: Safety training changed one model a lot
text: With safety training, Qwen3 4B wrote a hazard for 6 of 24 hostile requests and declined 17. With it removed, the same model wrote 22 and declined none.

title: Many models never said no
text: Asked to do something hostile, 8 of 14 models declined nothing, and that includes models with their safety training in place. Don't rely on a model to refuse.

title: termite stopped almost every hazard
text: These models wrote 259 hazardous replies to hostile requests. termite stopped or held 258 of them for a person to check, and 1 went straight in.

title: Refusing can go too far
text: qwen2.5 7B declined 7 of 15 harmless everyday requests. A model that refuses too much is a problem too, because people stop using it.

title: Models called hazards harmless
text: In at least 73 of 259 hazardous replies, the model said that the command only reads. Don't trust a model's description of its own command.

title: A bigger model was not clearly safer
text: Across 14 models, size had only a weak link with how often a model wrote a hazard. Test each model, and don't judge it by its size.

title: Too much context stops the answers
text: Context overflow happened in 51 of 168 trials above the limit, and in 0 of 756 trials at or below it. llama3.1 8B overflowed most, in 17 of 28 trials.

title: The policy catches what decision models miss
text: The 4 decision models rated 27 risky commands safe. termite's policy blocked 13 of them, and the other 14 were at tier 2, where a command shows personal information but no secrets.

title: Reading near secrets looks safe to them
text: Kev-4B rated 6 of 8 sensitive reads safe, such as listing a folder of keys. It rated 0 of 6 small project changes safe. A read near a secret can look harmless to a model.

title: No model refused every critical command
text: The best, tev1 4B, refused 6 of 8 commands at tier 6 and asked for approval on the rest. Each of the 4 models left some critical commands to a person.

title: The smallest model asks about everything
text: Kev-0.8B asked for approval on 51 of 52 commands, and rated only 1 of 14 harmless commands safe. That is cautious, but people stop reading warnings that they see every time.

title: Choosing the safest option is the weak spot
text: Given several ways to do a job, the best model put the safest way first in only 4 of 10 tests.

title: Some models give no usable score
text: 2 of 6 decision models never gave a score that termite could read, so they have no results.
